extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners in NLP, automated peer review, and scientific review process designers
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and evaluating automated scientific peer-review systems via a three-part framework (Standardization, Evaluation, Analysis) that produces constructive reviews and measures consistency between papers and reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEA framework (Standardization, Evaluation, Analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: A three-module automated paper reviewing framework (SEA) composed of SEA-S (Standardization), SEA-E (Evaluation), and SEA-A (Analysis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper proposes treating automated reviewing as three linked tasks: standardize heterogeneous review data, fine-tune models on standardized data to generate reviews, and analyze consistency between paper and generated reviews. This overall architecture is the organizing standard for the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data standardization capability (SEA-S)
rubrics_metrics.description: SEA-S distills data standardization capabilities of GPT-4 for integrating multiple reviews for a paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardization is evaluated by the ability to integrate multiple, heterogeneous human reviews into a consistent, structured representation usable for model training and downstream evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive review generation (SEA-E)
rubrics_metrics.description: SEA-E utilizes standardized data for fine-tuning, enabling it to generate constructive reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality of generated reviews is judged by constructiveness — i.e., whether reviews provide actionable, specific feedback useful for improving papers. SEA-E's purpose is to convert standardized review data into high-quality synthetic reviews via fine-tuning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mismatch score (consistency metric, SEA-A)
rubrics_metrics.description: A new evaluation metric called mismatch score to assess the consistency between paper contents and reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mismatch score quantifies how well review contents align with the paper's content; it is used as an objective measure in SEA-A to detect inconsistencies or hallucinations in reviews. The paper introduces this metric as a core analytic tool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-correction strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: A designed self-correction strategy to enhance the consistency between reviews and paper content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An iterative or corrective mechanism is applied to reduce mismatch score and improve review accuracy/consistency. The strategy is intended to refine generated reviews by identifying and correcting mismatches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usefulness / actionable insights for authors
rubrics_metrics.description: SEA can generate valuable insights for authors to improve their papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond consistency and fluency, a key evaluation dimension is whether the system's outputs provide actionable, specific suggestions that help authors revise and strengthen their manuscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-venue robustness / generalizability
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation on datasets collected from eight venues to demonstrate SEA's performance across different publication venues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A dimension of evaluation is generalizability: how well the standardization, generation, and analysis components perform across multiple venues and datasets, indicating robustness to domain/venue variation.
